Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork into dated document registers, assigning each intake a unique reference number, an applicant identifier, a document classification code, and a receipt timestamp. Files are routed through a case channel, indexed under the primary field names entered at intake, and sealed into the archive once the case status field is marked closed by an authorized clerk.

2) What occurred: The actor opened a document register file under an applicant identifier and recorded a document classification code for a union application. A named account was linked to the file via a field entry, and a dated record showing a transfer of value was appended to the case file. The actor created a set of supporting documents bearing relationship descriptions, each stamped with dates spanning multiple months. A second document register entry was prepared for a co-applicant, cross-referenced in a joint field on both files. The actor then scheduled a series of interview sessions and prepared written statements for both parties, filed as exhibit documents. A field on the primary application was marked to exclude a specific disclosure, and a routing note was added directing the file through a channel that bypassed a secondary review node. The file was sealed with the case status field set to closed.

3) Materials/access observed: A document register file, an applicant identifier, a named account, a dated transfer record, supporting documents with relationship description fields, exhibit documents containing written statements, a routing note, a channel designation, a secondary review node, and a case status field marked closed.

4) Indicators & artifacts: A dated transfer record appended to the case file with no corresponding declaration in the primary document fields. Multiple supporting documents bearing relationship descriptions with dates preceding the file opening date. A routing note designating a channel that bypasses a secondary review node. A field on the primary application marked to exclude a specific disclosure category. Written statements filed as exhibits with matching language patterns across both parties. A cross-reference field linking two document register entries under the same case.
